questions.question: What is the scientific term for a material that naturally attracts iron?
Which of the following is classified as a magnetic material?
How many distinct poles does a standard bar magnet possess?
What are the specific names given to the poles of a magnet?
Which of the following everyday materials will NOT be attracted to a magnet?
Where is the magnetic force geometrically strongest on a bar magnet?

options.text: Concentrated at the North and South poles

questions.question: What navigational device utilizes a freely suspended magnetic needle to find directions?
If you bring the North pole of one magnet near the South pole of another, what physical interaction occurs?
If you bring the North pole of one magnet near the North pole of another, what physical interaction occurs?
Can a permanent magnet be effectively used to separate iron filings from a pile of sand?

options.text: Only if the sand is wet

questions.question: If a bar magnet is suspended freely by a thread, in which geographic direction will it naturally align itself?
The painted tip of the needle in a standard magnetic compass always points towards which geographic direction?
What occurs if you physically break a bar magnet precisely into two halves?

options.text: You isolate one North pole piece and one South pole piece
You create two smaller, complete magnets, each possessing a North and a South pole
The magnetic force doubles in strength

questions.question: Which of the following elements/materials is completely non-magnetic?
How can you intentionally cause a permanent magnet to lose its magnetic properties (demagnetization)?

options.text: By washing it with pure water
By heating it strongly, dropping it repeatedly, or hammering it
By placing it in a freezer

questions.question: What is universally considered the surest test to definitively prove that a piece of metal is a magnet?
Why is repulsion considered the surest test of magnetism?

options.text: An ordinary iron bar will attract both poles of a magnet, but only another magnet will repel a specific pole
Repulsion is physically stronger than attraction

questions.question: A toy car has a hidden magnet inside. If the North pole of a testing bar magnet is repelled by the front of the car, what pole is located at the front of the car?
How should bar magnets be properly stored to ensure their magnetism is preserved over time?

options.text: Kept in pairs with opposite poles on the same side, separated by non-magnetic material, with soft iron keepers across the ends

questions.question: What specific material is commonly used to manufacture the sensitive needle of a navigation compass?
You are presented with two identical-looking metal bars. One is a magnet and one is plain iron. How can you identify the magnet using ONLY these two bars (no other tools or magnets allowed)?

options.text: It is scientifically impossible without a third reference magnet.
Touch the end of Bar A to the exact center of Bar B. If it sticks strongly, Bar A is the magnet.
Drop them simultaneously to gauge density.
Submerge them in water to check for oxidation rates.

questions.question: If a standard compass is placed very close to a strong permanent neodymium magnet, what will immediately happen to the compass needle?

options.text: It will continue pointing to Earth's magnetic North Pole accurately.
The needle will align itself with the localized magnetic field of the strong permanent magnet, overriding the Earth's weaker magnetic field.
It will spin in continuous circles.

questions.question: Why do iron filings sprinkled over a piece of stiff paper with a bar magnet placed underneath form a very specific, symmetrical curved pattern?

options.text: The filings physically align themselves along the invisible magnetic field lines generated by the magnet.
Iron filings are naturally manufactured in curved shapes.

questions.question: In ancient history, what naturally occurring magnetic mineral was discovered by early navigators and utilized as the first primitive compass?

Logical deduction: If the South pole of Magnet A attracts an unknown pole of Magnet B, and that same unknown pole of Magnet B repels the North pole of Magnet C, what is the identity of the unknown pole?
Why do precision compasses not point exactly to the true geographic North Pole of the Earth?

options.text: Because the Earth's magnetic north pole is physically offset and constantly shifting slightly relative to the geographic axis of rotation.
Because commercial compasses are poorly calibrated.
Because the needle is too heavy to point perfectly straight.
Solar winds push the needle off course.

questions.question: What is the underlying physical purpose of an "iron keeper" used when storing permanent magnets?

options.text: To prevent the magnets from rusting by blocking oxygen.
To provide a closed, highly permeable path for the magnetic field lines, which prevents self-demagnetization over time.
To increase the physical weight of the magnets to prevent movement.

questions.question: How does a magnet successfully separate a dry mixture of iron filings and yellow sulfur powder?

options.text: The magnet chemically dissolves the sulfur.
The magnetic force physically attracts the iron filings out of the mixture, leaving the non-magnetic sulfur powder behind.
The magnet generates wind to blow the sulfur away.
The sulfur becomes magnetic via induction.

questions.question: Which of the following actions will absolutely NOT result in the demagnetization of a permanent magnet?

options.text: Heating it in an open fire.
Dropping it repeatedly onto a concrete floor.
Painting its surface with standard watercolor paint.
Striking it repeatedly with a heavy hammer.

questions.question: If you stroke a permanent magnet along the length of an ordinary soft iron nail repeatedly, lifting the magnet away at the end of each stroke and moving in the same direction, what happens to the nail?

options.text: Its internal magnetic domains align, and it temporarily becomes magnetized itself.
